verdict.rationale: Unreal Engine ships extensive first-party support for editor extensibility: Python scripting of the editor for asset automation and custom UIs (unreal-docs-4, unreal-docs-28, unreal-docs-29), a Blutility/Scripting-and-Automating framework for repeating tasks and custom editor utilities (unreal-docs-26, unreal-docs-35), a full Plugin system that extends Editor capabilities (unreal-docs-5, unreal-docs-13), C++ editor modules/Blueprint function libraries with EditorScripting metadata (unreal-docs-33), and even a Remote Control REST/WebSocket API to drive editor/asset functions externally (unreal-docs-22, unreal-docs-23, unreal-docs-24). This covers scripting, plugins, and programmatic scene/asset manipulation comprehensively. Missing for 10: independent hands-on case studies specifically validating Python/editor-scripting workflows (community evidence mostly concerns gameplay scripting/C++ rather than editor tooling directly).
